flags.reason: An earlier confirmatory experiment in the same paper (Section 2) used 5 different subjects; n_subjects here reflects the larger, primary verification experiment (10 subjects) described in Section 3 onward.
Stimuli were broadband high-resolution audio recordings with ultrasonic content above 20 kHz rather than a single carrier frequency; no discrete kHz value is stated.

This is airborne/air-conducted sound presented via loudspeaker to the ear, not a transducer-based transcranial or bone-conducted ultrasound exposure; no target id in the vocabulary matches, so 'other' was used.

Section 2.1 explicitly states stimulus presentation order was NOT random; Section 3's description ('the order... was changed for each measurement') does not explicitly say random, so randomised was left not_reported rather than assumed true or false.

readout_other: log power spectrum (alpha/beta band) and nonlinear chaos-based features (maximum Lyapunov index, sample entropy, permutation entropy) of scalp EEG; SVM-based verification (equal error rate, EER)
direction_notes: Alpha-band EEG power tended to increase (rather than decrease or stay unchanged) around 20 s after the start of inaudible (>20 kHz) ultrasonic stimulus presentation, and personal (familiar) ultrasonic stimuli evoked more individually distinctive EEG responses than unrelated or common ultrasonic stimuli.

exposures.label: Inaudible (>20 kHz) ultrasonic components of airborne audio stimuli

target.label: brain/auditory system, via air-conducted inaudible high-frequency sound presented through a loudspeaker

timing.protocol_description: High-resolution audio (96 kHz sampling, 24-bit) containing ultrasonic components above 20 kHz was presented through a loudspeaker; in the first experiment (5 subjects) both-audible-and-ultrasound (BOT), audible-only (AUD) and ultrasound-only (ULT) stimuli were each presented for 240 s with 120 s silent intervals between. In the second experiment (10 subjects), a personal ultrasonic stimulus (P), an unrelated ultrasound (U) and a common ultrasound (C) were each presented for 30 s with 120 s silent intervals, repeated over 10 measurements per subject; sound level was adjusted to approximately 70 dB near the ear.
